newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 27.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
CHOSUN ILBO
- North Korea agreed to attend four-way peace talks if
it receives emergency food aid.
- Bus fare may be raised 30 won to reach 430 won after
April.
JOONG ANG ILBO
- Main opposition National Congress for New Politics party
leader Kim Dae-jung is expected to suggest to President Kim
Young-sam a meeting with the three main party leaders for
next week.
KOREA TIMES
- President Kim Young-sam on Wednesday made it clear that
there will be no consitutional revision during the remainder
of his term, flatly rejecting a call for the introduction of
a parliamentary cabinet system from the political circles.
- A delegation of five U.S. Congressmen headed by Ted
Stevens, chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee,
arrived in Seoul on Wednesday, kicking off their four-day
inter-Korean trip.
MAEIL BUSINESS NEWSPAPER
- Samsung Group has allocated 2.5 trillion won to reseach
and development this year.
